newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland expects $1 bln from privatisation in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Poland expects $1 bln from privatisation in 1997.

text.p: Poland has earned $1 billion from privatisation this year and wants to raise another billion in 1997, the deputy privatisation minister said on Thursday.
Ewa Feyberg told an international conference on investment in Poland that since the start of market reforms in 1990 almost 4,500 out of 8,500 state-owned companies had been sold.
"The target for 1996 and for 1997 is one billion dollars," Freyberg said.

"The 1996 target has already been reached and we should have no problems with raising the same amount of cash next year, as some one quarter of it would come solely from the sale of the KGHM copper concern", she added.

Freyberg said the other big firms earmarked for near-term sale were Bank Handlowy SA, to be privatised in the frist half of 1997, Polish airlines LOT, the Katowice steel mill and the Orbis tourism company. @

She said the privatisations and the flotation of mass privatisation National Investment Fund (NFI) shares on the Warsaw bourse early next year would boost the stock exchange's capitalisation by more than one third.
"The capitalisation of the bourse is currently at around $9 billion, and the flotation of the NFI shares will increase it by about one third next year," Freyberg said.

Under Poland's mass privatisation programme 15 NFIs run 512 companies. Each adult Pole is entitled to buy for 20 zlotys a participation certificate in the programme, which will later be exchanged for one share of each of the funds. @

Freyberg said that between 40 and 50 new firms were likely to enter the Warsaw bourse next year, many of which would come from the National Investment Fund (NFI) programme -- floated by their parent NFI.

She also said many firms from the NFI programme would become listed on the over-the-counter market, expected to start trade later this year, and increase investment possiblities for foreign and domestic investors.
